Each icon has gradients, outlines and marks, but you set only one accent color. Every other tone is calculated from it in CSS, so recoloring, theming and dark mode come down to setting that one color and, if you like, a variant.

Each icon plays its motion on hover, with the same <0>trigger</0>, <1>hover</1> and <2>title</2> props as the layered icons. A lid swings open, a page is torn off, a letter comes out of its envelope. Parts that only appear on hover are hidden in the server-rendered markup, so they never flash before the script runs. With reduced motion turned on, icons go straight to their end pose.

Each icon plays its motion on hover, with the same <0>trigger</0>, <1>hover</1> and <2>title</2> props as the other styles. Where it can, the motion changes the icon's state: a lock's shackle lifts open, a bookmark ribbon grows down, a trash can's lid lifts and a slash draws across the icon it turns off. Some move parts in depth while the outline stays still: a globe's meridians turn round it, the pages of an open book turn over, a laptop's screen closes on its hinge; strokes keep their width throughout.
